This is unprecedented:

2026 is currently on track to become the only calendar year in at least 30 years with zero 80%+ NYSE downside-volume days.

These are days when at least 80% of NYSE trading volume comes from declining stocks, signaling unusually broad-based selling pressure.

By comparison, 2008 had 49 such days during the Financial Crisis, versus 33 during the 2022 bear market and just 9 last year.

Meanwhile, the average since 1997 is 21 such trading days, with no calendar year ever recording fewer than 5.

In other words, broad-based selling pressure has been almost nonexistent so far in 2026.

The market is more resilient than ever.

One clarification on the $24.7M/MW, since some might read it as an annual number. It is not.

The $105B is a lifetime cap on the whole deal. Divided by 4,250 MW, that is the most NVIDIA could ever pay per megawatt, total.

How the payment works: The Agreements specify a guaranteed minimum value (undisclosed so far) for each lease. If OpenAI defaults or goes insolvent, SB Energy re-lets or sells the space, and NVIDIA pays the shortfall between that guaranteed minimum and what the re-let or sale brings in.

What we do not know is what sets the guaranteed minimum. It could either be the rent remaining on the lease, or what the building cost to construct. A rent-based promise shrinks as OpenAI pays. A cost-based one may not shrink at all.

Testing the rent case: NVIDIA stands behind this lease, so it should discount closer to an investment-grade cost of capital than to an equity rate. At 6-8%, the NOI Portsmouth needs to justify a $24.7M/MW promise over 20 years is $2.15-2.52M/MW/year.

RIOT's Rockdale lease is the most recent public comp. 191 MW, 20 years, $9.1B of contract revenue and $365-411M average annual NOI per the company, or roughly $2.0M/MW/year. Portsmouth would need to price 8-25% above that for the remaining rent to equal $24.7M/MW at the start of the lease. Seems entirely plausible for greenfield with a 20-year term. So the rent case holds up.

The cost case also fits. $24.7M/MW lines up with the $25-31M/MW it takes to build the non-silicon half of a greenfield campus.

The Agreement will get filed with NVIDIA's 10-Q later this month and settle the logic.

Open to other interpretations. Any ideas?

Testing the rent case: NVIDIA stands behind this lease, so it should discount closer to an investment-grade cost of capital than to an equity rate. At 6-8%, the NOI Portsmouth needs to justify a $24.7M/MW promise over 20 years is $2.15-2.52M/MW/year.

RIOT's Rockdale lease is the most recent public comp. 191 MW, 20 years, $9.1B of contract revenue and $365-411M average annual NOI per the company, or roughly $2.0M/MW/year. Portsmouth would need to price 8-25% above that for the remaining rent to equal $24.7M/MW at the start of the lease. Seems entirely plausible for greenfield with a 20-year term. So the rent case holds up.

The cost case also fits. $24.7M/MW lines up with the $25-31M/MW it takes to build the non-silicon half of a greenfield campus.

The Agreement will get filed with NVIDIA's 10-Q later this month and settle the logic.
